title: AC vs. Heat Pump: Which is Better for Your Home? | Comprehensive Comparison
channel: Monkey Wrench Plumbing, Heating, Air & Electric
summary: Los Angeles HVAC company compares air-source heat pumps with air conditioners on cooling, efficiency ratings, price, installation and maintenance.

assertions.quote: Heat pumps and air conditioners have similar energy efficiency ratings.
heat pumps can provide heating and cooling, whereas ACs only provide cooling
air source heat pumps tend to cost thousands of dollars more than air conditioners
a heat pump installation can also cost more if your home doesn't have the proper electrical panel upgrades to support it
if you're looking to replace your cooling system and keep your furnace, then a new air conditioner is ideal

verdicts.note: An AC is usually somewhat cheaper upfront, though a heat pump paired with the furnace adds dual-fuel savings for a modest premium.
Wholesale heat pumps cost $200-$500 more than equivalently sized air conditioners.
Edwards' national installed-cost medians are $4,684 for a central AC and $6,185 for a heat pump of the same size.
In the NREL cost database the efficient AC is cheaper than the efficient heat pump ($5,180 vs $5,550), but at base efficiency the heat pump is slightly cheaper ($2,994 vs $3,164).

assertions.quote: heat pumps need an additional maintenance checkup before the start of the cold weather season
these systems can be powered through solar panels to help offset some of the operating costs
